On this page

Availability Search for a Single Entry ​

This page explains how to allow your users to inquire about the availability and price of a single Entry.

Usage ​

Usually, you'll use this on the Entry's page, in a sidebar or a modal. To offer you the most flexibility, we've split the search and results parts into separate components. That way, you can better customize the layout to fit your needs.

So, let's say you have a cruise named "Three Islands Cruise" and you want to allow your users to book tickets. A basic example would look like this:

antlers
<div class="max-w-md">
    <div class="my-8">
        {{ livewire:availability-search enableQuantity="true" :rates="true" :entry="id" }}
    </div>
    <div class="my-8">
        {{ livewire:availability-results :entry="id" :rates="true" }}
    </div>
</div>

Here, we have an AvailabilitySearch component with rates and quantity enabled. Passing :entry="id" lets the search resolve the per-entry rate labels for the dropdown. The results are displayed in a separate AvailabilityResults component, which must also receive :rates="true" to show the rate-based UI.

Display availability in the calendar ​

When inside an entry, you may want to display the availability plan (pricing & available items) for that entry. To do this, enable the showAvailabilityOnCalendar parameter and pass the entry's ID, for example:

antlers
{{ livewire:availability-search showAvailabilityOnCalendar="true" :entry="id" }}

Resrv takes care of the rest for you:

INFO

When rates are also enabled, the calendar shows availability only after a specific rate is picked, since pricing and availability depend on the selected rate.

Error handling ​

The component will display relevant information or error messages if the user fails to set all the required search fields (in this example, date & rate) or if there is no availability.

What's next? ​

You can now move to the AvailabilityResults component to customize the results shown or check out how to search for multiple available entries.
